issues.legal_issue: A recipient that possesses land openly and continuously under an ineffective rent-free grant can acquire by prescription a limited right to hold the land on the grant’s terms, including immunity from assessment.
material_facts: The government authorized a rent-free grant of land for use as a market, but the required formalities for an effective grant were not completed.
The recipient took possession under the purported grant and, with its predecessor, openly and uninterruptedly held the land as of right for more than the applicable limitation period.
The recipient gave up the former market sites and spent substantial sums preparing the land and constructing and maintaining market buildings.
The land continued to be used for the market purpose for which the grant had been authorized, and no rent or assessment was paid during the long period of possession.
issues.conclusion: The recipient acquired a limited right to hold the land in perpetuity, rent-free and only for the authorized market purpose. The immunity from rent was part of that acquired right and limited the government’s power to assess the land; the assessment was therefore not permitted.
issues.legal_principle: Under section 8 of the Bombay City Land Revenue Act, an established and preserved specific limit on assessment restricts the assessment that may be levied. Although the purported grant was ineffective for want of statutory formalities, possession under its color that continued openly, uninterruptedly and as of right for the applicable limitation period could establish the limited title the recipient had been prescribing for. The acquired title included the grant’s rent-free term and its restriction to the stated use. The court relied on Goswamini Shri Kamalavahooji v. Collector of Bombay in holding that section 8 can protect a total exemption, with nil as the specific limit.

rule.if: assessment_challenge_proceeding and authorized_rent_free_grant and ineffective_formal_transfer and possession_under_purported_grant and open_uninterrupted_possession_as_of_right and possession_beyond_limitation_period and land_used_for_authorized_purpose

predicates.assessment_challenge_proceeding: A proceeding challenges a government assessment imposed on land.
predicates.authorized_rent_free_grant: The government authorized the recipient to hold the land without rent for a specified purpose.
predicates.ineffective_formal_transfer: The purported transfer did not satisfy the required formalities and therefore did not itself convey an effective title.
predicates.possession_under_purported_grant: The recipient took possession of the land on the basis of the purported grant.
predicates.open_uninterrupted_possession_as_of_righ: The recipient possessed the land openly, continuously and as of right.
predicates.possession_beyond_limitation_period: The recipient’s possession continued beyond the applicable limitation period.
predicates.land_used_for_authorized_purpose: The recipient used the land for the purpose specified in the purported grant.

issues.definition: When an assessment challenge concerns land possessed beyond the applicable limitation period under an ineffective rent-free grant and used for its specified purpose, the rule bars assessment to the extent of the rent-free right acquired by prescription.

issues.legal_issue: A specific limit on assessment under the applicable land-revenue scheme can be nil, so the scheme’s protection of a preserved limit includes a total exemption.
material_facts: The government resolution stated that no rent should be charged for land authorized for use as a public market.
The recipient claimed that the authorized grant exempted the land entirely from assessment.
The government sought to assess the land despite the claimed exemption.
issues.conclusion: The applicable limit may be nil; a total exemption from assessment falls within the protection for a specific limit on assessment.
issues.legal_principle: Section 8 of the Bombay City Land Revenue Act protects a superior holder’s right where a specific limit to assessment has been established and preserved. Following Goswamini Shri Kamalavahooji v. Collector of Bombay, the court held that this includes a total exemption, for which the specific limit is nil.

predicates.assessment_challenge_proceeding: A proceeding challenges a government assessment imposed on land.
predicates.assessment_scheme_protects_preserved_spe: The governing assessment scheme limits assessment when a specific limit has been established and preserved.
predicates.total_exemption_from_assessment_is_estab: The holder establishes a right that no assessment is payable on the land.

issues.definition: When a proceeding challenges an assessment under a scheme that protects preserved limits, an established total exemption is treated as a protected specific limit.

issues.legal_issue: A party cannot introduce for the first time at the appellate stage an unpleaded distinction between rent and land revenue when that distinction was not raised or tried below and the record treated the terms as including one another.
material_facts: The government’s resolution provided that no rent would be charged for the land.

The recipient asserted before the assessment dispute reached the Supreme Court that rent, in the relevant official usage, included land revenue, and the government did not deny that assertion in its reply.
The government did not plead the distinction between rent and land revenue, the distinction was not made an issue at trial, and it was not advanced in the courts below.
issues.conclusion: The government could not raise the distinction at that stage; for deciding the case, rent was treated as synonymous with or including land revenue.
issues.legal_principle: An appellate party may not introduce a new contention that was not pleaded, made an issue, or raised in the courts below. Because the assertion that rent included land revenue was not denied in the record, the court proceeded on that basis for this case.

rule.if: assessment_appeal and rent_revenue_distinction_not_pleaded and rent_revenue_distinction_not_tried_below and record_does_not_deny_rent_includes_revenue

predicates.assessment_appeal: An appeal concerns a government assessment imposed on land.
predicates.rent_revenue_distinction_not_pleaded: The party seeking to distinguish rent from land revenue did not raise that distinction in its pleadings.
predicates.rent_revenue_distinction_not_tried_below: The distinction was not made an issue or argued before the lower courts.
predicates.record_does_not_deny_rent_includes_reven: The record contains an assertion that rent includes land revenue that the opposing party did not deny.

issues.definition: In an assessment appeal, a party cannot obtain consideration of a rent-and-revenue distinction that was neither pleaded nor tried below when the record does not deny that rent includes revenue.
